claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 normally requires sintering above 2300 °C.
ZrB2 variants prepared at approximately 1700 °C have insufficient oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
The proposed intervention is addition of approximately 1–3 wt% silicon powder to the ZrB2 precursor.
Adding 1–3 wt% silicon will permit ZrB2 densification at around 1700 °C in an inert or reducing atmosphere.
Silicon addition will form a silica-rich intergranular phase in situ.
The silica-rich intergranular phase will promote densification.
The silica-rich intergranular phase will act as a barrier to oxygen penetration.
The silica-rich intergranular phase will act as a barrier to liquid plating-metal penetration.
Silicon lowers the effective sintering temperature through transient liquid-phase sintering.
A protective silica layer forms at grain boundaries during processing and service.
The grain-boundary silica layer reduces oxidation rates.
The grain-boundary silica layer reduces liquid-metal corrosion rates.
Si-doped ZrB2 sintered near 1700 °C will have mechanical strength and structural integrity similar to or better than single-phase ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
Si-doped ZrB2 will have significantly greater oxidation resistance than both high-temperature-sintered single-phase ZrB2 and lower-temperature specimens without silicon.
Si-doped ZrB2 will have significantly greater liquid-metal corrosion durability than both high-temperature-sintered single-phase ZrB2 and lower-temperature specimens without silicon.
The anticipated service boundary includes oxidizing exposure at approximately 1200–1500 °C and controlled liquid plating baths.
Performance outside the stated processing and service boundaries remains unverified.
The magnitude of oxidation and corrosion improvement may vary with silicon content, sintering conditions, and service environment.
